title: Platform capability registry
description: Machine-readable statement of what each supported harness can actually do. Skills declare the capabilities they require and the ones they merely prefer; this registry is the only place that answers whether a given target provides them. Every platform must carry an explicit entry for every capability key — an omitted key is a schema error, not an implied 'no', so a gap can never be hidden by silence.

last_reviewed.description: Date this registry was last checked against the platforms it describes.

capability_definitions.description: One entry per capability key, defining what the capability means. The key set here is the contract; platform entries must cover exactly it.

degradation.description: What a skill should do when this capability is absent.

platforms.description: One entry per supported target, keyed by the same snake_case id used in docs/engineering/build-and-release/platform-targets.json.

status.description: native = first-class platform feature. native-experimental = shipped but behind a flag or documented as unstable. partial = present with material limits, spelled out in notes. emulated = the framework builds it from lower-level primitives (usually shell + git). adapter = provided through a platform-specific translation layer rather than the canonical artifact. unsupported = verified absent; skills must degrade. unknown = not verified — treat as unsupported at runtime and never advertise it.

since.description: Version floor at which the capability became available on this platform.

validation.description: Command that proves the status claim. Required for anything claimed as native or native-experimental — evidence over declarations.

fallback.description: What the framework does instead when this capability is not available here.

allOf.$comment: A native claim without a validation command is a declaration, not evidence.
Anything short of native must say what happens instead.

aliases.description: Other spellings of this platform id that consumers may encounter (kebab-case, marketing names). Present so every consumer normalizes the same way instead of inventing its own mapping.

doc_urls.description: Authoritative upstream documentation for this platform. Kept in sync with the doc_urls array in docs/engineering/build-and-release/platform-targets.json; consumers such as platform-sync should prefer this over their own bundled URL lists.

runtime_surface_of.description: Set when this target is a runtime surface of another adapter rather than a distinct distribution format (Claude Desktop consumes the Claude Code plugin).

capabilities.description: Every capability key must be present. Use status 'unknown' for anything unverified rather than omitting it.
